build_check.description: index.html and game_logic.js exist, a canvas/WebGL renderer is present, and no disallowed heavy runtime asset references are used.

requirements.description: Turn-based card combat: the player draws cards each turn, has limited energy to spend, and plays attack cards to deal damage or skill cards to gain block. Cards are dragged or clicked to play them. Energy cost is shown on each card and deducted on play. The turn ends when the player clicks an end-turn button. Score 0 if combat is not turn-based, if there is no energy system, or if cards cannot be played interactively.

Enemies display their intent before the player's turn: an icon or text shows whether they will attack (with damage number), buff themselves, or debuff the player. The player uses this information to decide whether to attack or defend. Block absorbs incoming damage and resets each turn. Score 0 if enemy intent is hidden, if there is no block mechanic, or if the player cannot react to enemy plans.

After combat, the player chooses 1 of 3 offered cards to add to their deck (or skips). Cards have rarities (Common/Uncommon/Rare) with distinct visual borders or colours. A branching map shows the path through the act with different node types (combat, elite, shop, rest, event). The player chooses their route. Score 0 if there is no card reward, if there is no map, or if the path is linear with no choice.

At least 3 character classes with different starting decks, card pools, and signature mechanics. Each class has a unique portrait and thematic identity. The player selects their class before starting a run. Score 0 if there is only one class, if classes share the same cards, or if there is no class selection.

At least 20 distinct cards across the card pool with different effects (damage, block, draw, buff, debuff, multi-hit, conditional). Each card has a name, energy cost, description, and rarity. Cards feel mechanically distinct from each other. Score 0 if there are fewer than 20 cards, if cards are functionally identical, or if card text is missing.

Relics (passive items) modify rules and are displayed in a relic bar. At least 5 distinct relics exist with unique effects. Elite enemies always drop a relic. Relics have tooltip descriptions on hover. Score 0 if there are no relics, if fewer than 5 exist, or if relics have no visible display.

The run spans at least 3 acts, each ending with a boss that has unique mechanics and multi-phase patterns. Bosses are visually distinct from regular enemies with larger sprites and special attack animations. Defeating the final boss wins the run with a victory screen. Score 0 if there is only one act, if bosses behave like regular enemies, or if there is no victory condition.

The combat screen clearly shows: player health, enemy health, player energy, hand of cards (readable text), enemy intent icons, block amount, and relic bar. All elements are non-overlapping and readable at 1280x720. Score 0 if any core element is missing or unreadable.

Card play produces visible effects: attack cards show damage numbers and hit animations on the enemy; block cards show a shield icon appearing on the player; buffs/debuffs show status icons. The player can assess the board state from any single frame. Score 0 if card play has no visual feedback, or if damage/block is not animated.

The full game loop is connected: Title -> Class select -> Map navigation -> Combat -> Card reward -> Shop/rest -> Boss -> Victory or death. The player can experience every node without restarting. Score 0 if any transition in the chain is missing or broken.

A title screen is present and styled: it shows the game name in a custom or themed font, has at minimum a play button that is interactive and transitions to class select, and uses a non-default background (dark tower, fantasy landscape, or card artwork) — not plain plain grey or a solid-colour fill. Score 0 if the game launches directly into gameplay with no title screen, or if the start button is non-functional. Full credit may be earned with runtime-authored procedural textures, layered materials, deliberate multi-light rigs, particles, synthesized audio, or post-processing; external asset files are not required.

Overall art-style coherence: every visible element — cards, enemies, map nodes, UI panels, relics — belongs to a single consistent visual language. The palette is dark fantasy themed; no clashing styles or unrelated assets. Score 0 if the screen mixes incompatible styles, or if elements are obviously unthemed placeholder shapes.

Cards have illustrated art, borders, and readable text; enemies have distinct detailed sprites; the map uses themed node icons; UI panels and buttons use styled widgets with custom fonts; relics have unique icons. Score 0 if cards are plain text boxes, if enemies are solid-colour primitives, or if UI is unstyled defaults.

Animation continuity and polish: card draw, card play, damage numbers, enemy attack animations, block shield appearance, status effect application, map transitions, and screen changes each play as smooth multi-frame tweens or sprite animations. No element snaps to its new state in a single frame. Transitions use fades or slides. Score 0 if any of these moments is instantaneous, or if transitions are hard cuts.
